note: Binary judge items with evidence, per format (research notes R1, R2, R3, R4, R10 and V2 to V6, 2026-09-26). Each item is asked as a yes or no question about the draft; the majority of six votes decides. Hard fails stop delivery whatever the other items say.

items.question: Does it serve the brief's stated goal with the matching call to action (said aloud as well as shown, for video), answer every audience objection the brief lists, and add no detail (a prop, place, time, motive or number) that the brief or the research does not hold?
Do the title, the thumbnail idea, the first 30 seconds and the payoff make one promise, and does the payoff deliver it (at least as big as the package)?

Does the opening confirm the topic within about 25 words and give a specific stake or a turn (but, except, yet) within about 20 seconds, with no greeting, logo, subscribe ask or sponsor in the first 30 seconds?
Are the beats chained by but or therefore (cause and consequence), not by and-then, with every opened question paid off later?
Is there a turn that reframes the question around 40 to 55 percent of the runtime, and a re-engagement at least every 3 to 4 minutes after that?
For an explainer: is the common misconception stated and then refuted (not only the correct explanation given)? Answer pass when the piece is not an explainer.
Are the stakes concrete (who loses or gains what) and stated before the midpoint?
Does every section carry concrete detail (a number, name, date, place or object), with the key facts sourced, not vague 'experts say'?
Does it read aloud cleanly at speaking pace: short spoken sentences, varied rhythm, numbers said the way people say them?
Does every one to three sentences have a concrete visual to show (not generic 'b-roll'), shown before it is told where possible?
Does it sound like one real creator with a point of view, with none of the machine tells (template openers, 'let's dive in', stock phrases, a moral at the end, named emotions, rule-of-three tics)?
Does it end on the payoff and one call to action tied to a next video, without a recap, a stated moral or a wind-down that signals the end early?
Does every section earn its minutes (no padding, no point made twice)?

Is there a first turning point (the event that flips the starting situation) in roughly the first quarter and a second turn around 75 to 85 percent of the runtime, each clearly caused rather than sudden?
Is there at least one moment the viewer can see, slowed down at the turn, with concrete detail (the place, an action, an exact spoken line or thought), rather than a summary?
Does every section end on a forward pull (an open question, a contrast or a tease that is later paid), so the viewer always knows the next step?
Do names, places, amounts, products and ages stay the same from start to end (no drift)?
Do the references, units, money, register, address form and humour feel native to the audience in the brief, and respectful of elders, faith, gender and the people shown?

Is every factual claim, number, quote, date and place either sourced or given in the brief, with reconstructions and composites marked, and free of pop-science claims (dopamine hits, oxytocin, 22 times more memorable, goldfish attention)?

hard_fails: the package and the payoff do not match
an unsourced or invented key fact
a banned phrase in the first 30 seconds
the title's question is never answered
a continuity error (a name, place, amount or product changes midway)
an invented event, quote or person presented as real
a hook the body contradicts

Is there at least one concrete, checkable detail (a number, name, place or object) and one real surprise that was set up fairly?
Does it sound like a real creator on this platform, free of machine tells and greetings?
Does the story work with the sound off (on-screen text carries it) and with the sound on?
Does the length, pace and format fit the platform (native look, captions in short chunks)?
Does one event flip the situation by about a third of the runtime, after only the setup the viewer needs to feel it?
Do names, places, amounts, products and ages stay the same from start to end (no drift)?
Do the references, units, money, register, address form and humour feel native to the audience in the brief, and respectful of elders, faith, gender and the people shown?

Is every factual claim, number, quote, date and place either sourced or given in the brief, with reconstructions and composites marked, and free of pop-science claims (dopamine hits, oxytocin, 22 times more memorable, goldfish attention)?
